FRONT VIEW

FRONT FULL-BODY VIEW

FRONT | 3/4 LEFT | LEFT PROFILE | 3/4 RIGHT | BACK

ALL 10 FRAMES MUST SHOW EXACTLY THE SAME PERSON.

Maintain identical:
- Face
- Hair
- Hairline
- Hair color
- Facial proportions
- Body proportions
- Height
- Physique
- Skin tone

- Accessories

==================================================

Use one simple, clean, fitted outfit suitable for a professional character/model reference sheet.

The EXACT SAME outfit must appear in all 10 frames.

Do not change clothing between panels.

Do not change hairstyle between panels.

FACE FRAMES:

FULL-BODY FRAMES:

第1003期 小路和你读AI论文。今日4篇高质量论文。

1. 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗦𝗮𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴: 𝗦𝗙𝗧 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻𝘀 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸（《带采样的微调：SFT 比你想的更会学》）

链接：https://t.co/QXVXbqz5hu

作者背景：Aayush Karan, Sitan Chen, Yilun Du, Harvard

不改损失，用 MCMC 把离策略专家轨迹逐步改写成更接近参考模型的在策略分布，SFT 在泛化与遗忘上就能比肩强在策略后训练。实验覆盖科学技能、数学推理和开放式专长。采样本身可以当作后训练原语，这会动摇"保能力必须上 RL"的默认做法，做后训练的人值得细看。

2. 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗙𝗶𝘁: 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹-𝗛𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗔𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗧𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀（《找到合适的搭配：跨 Agent 任务的模型与 Harness 交互》）

链接：https://t.co/txmUWsp8E5

作者背景：Yixuan Li, Bo An 等

模型、harness 与任务必须放在一起评，强模型和厂商自有脚手架都不会稳定领先。66 组配置横跨 OpenHands、DeepSeek Harness、PI、openJiuwen 与三项命令行 agent 基准。Terminal-Bench 4 上，Claude 在 OpenHands 中领先 GPT 7.94 分，在 PI 中落后 30.16 分，五个模型里有四个的最优 harness 随基准改变。作者发布了适配器、评测代码和 6,204 条轨迹，部署 agent 的人可以直接拿来做选型证据。

3. 𝗛𝗶𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝘂𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗗𝗶𝗳𝗳𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗴𝘂𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗠𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹𝘀（《分层连续扩散语言模型》）

链接：https://t.co/dC0fv3j4PU

作者背景：Alexander Schwing（UIUC）等

让连续潜变量成为唯一持续生成状态，token 每步读出并回馈，以缓解离散扩散并行解码时的独立采样断裂。训练目标来自 token 似然的变分界，同规模下在 Sudoku、Countdown 和 LM1B 上优于离散与连续扩散基线。做扩散语言模型的人可以看看它是否真正保住了并行解码中的 token 依赖。

4. 𝗘𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘆 𝗔𝗯𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗜𝘀 𝗮 𝗗𝗼𝘀𝗲: 𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘄𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗦𝗲𝗹𝗳-𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗿（《每次消融都是一剂药：反权重与"自修复"的假象》）

链接：https://t.co/IzLv2zqidD

消融后看似补偿的响应，多半来自干预前就存在的反权重，它们随对比强度作仿射响应，与临时自我修复无关。在事实判决任务上，Gemma、Qwen、LLaMA、Mistral 的 81 个下游方向中有 68 个服从该仿射律。GPT-2 Small 的 IOI 电路里，干预能触及的 10 个头有 7 个符合，且全是反权重，斜率还能由固定权重预先估计。做机制可解释性的人可以拿它校准对自修复的判断。

PROMPT SHARE: The biggest AI breakthrough isn’t realism. It’s presence.

#AIVideo #Marketing #Advertising

The people, movement, noise and unpredictability give the world a sense of life beyond the camera.

That’s when generation starts becoming experience.

➜ Image Prompt:

Photography & Cinematography
Create an ultra-realistic nighttime street portrait with the raw, spontaneous look of early-2000s nightlife photography. Direct on-camera flash illuminates the subject sharply against a much darker city background, with natural grain, slight highlight blowout, deep shadows, imperfect exposure and authentic point-and-shoot character. No fake or plastic skin, no beauty filtering, no CGI or animated appearance.

Character & Pose
A striking young man with rugged, high-fashion model features, lean athletic build, sharply defined jawline and cheekbones, strong brows, full lips and short dark hair styled wet and tousled with loose curls falling onto his forehead. Natural pores, subtle facial texture and realistic imperfections. He sits casually on the edge of a city curb at night, legs spread asymmetrically, one knee raised toward the camera. One forearm rests loosely across the raised knee while his other hand reaches down beside him toward a small shaggy brown dog partially entering the bottom of the frame. He looks directly into the camera with a serious, confident expression.

Outfit
Fitted black long-sleeve turtleneck, faded distressed gray-blue jeans with worn areas and small rips, and a black leather belt. Silver pendant necklace, small hoop earring, chunky silver cuff bracelet, dark oversized wristwatch, and a thin bracelet. Styling feels slightly rebellious, understated and naturally lived-in rather than polished.

Environment
A busy urban nightlife street after dark. Several casually dressed people walk behind him, cropped naturally by the frame, while parked and passing cars create scattered headlights and small pools of distant light. The pavement is gritty and imperfect with curbs, cracks and ordinary street details visible. Keep the background activity believable and incidental—the image should feel like a real moment caught outside a club or late-night gathering, not a staged fashion shoot. Wide horizontal composition, intimate close-range flash photography, authentic real-world energy.

Without automatic QC, is an AI image pipeline actually worth it?

I'm starting to think the honest answer is: 
.. not really.

Generation is fast now. Checking isn't. If people still have to inspect every image by hand, you haven't automated production. You've moved the bottleneck from the photo studio to the review queue.

A while ago I was talking with Matthias Haase and his team in Zalando about what it really takes to scale GenAI content. We kept coming back to one point: the value is not in one clever generation. It's in automating the whole pipeline, end to end.

And manual review is not enough. An AI image can look perfect and still be wrong. One button becomes two. Tonal stitching turns into contrast stitching. The logo is almost right, which on a product page means it's wrong. Nobody notices on image 180 of 200. The customer notices when the parcel arrives.

Think about it this way: every fashion brand runs QC on its products before they ship. Nobody would ship 10,000 polos without checking that the buttons match the spec. So why publish 10,000 images with nothing more than a quick look at the thumbnails?

That's why we built automatic quality control into On-Model. Every generated image is compared with your own product photos: colour, cut, closures, trims, logos, and consistency across the whole set. It flags the few images worth a second look and stays quiet when everything matches. People review only what needs attention and still make the final call.

You save on the shoot, then pay it back in review hours and returns. Without QC, that's not ROI. It's just moving the cost somewhere else.

So, for those already using AI for product images: how many hours does your team spend checking them? And do you trust what gets through?

几乎所有 reward model 都在做同一个简化：把人类偏好压成一个分数。

但真实的人类反馈往往不是一个点——同一个回答，不同人可以给出不同、甚至互相冲突的判断。把多峰偏好硬压成标量，模型学到的只是"平均值"，而不是"人们到底怎么想"。

清华 THUNLP 的新工作 DRM（Diffusion Reward Model）换了个问法：能不能让奖励模型学人类偏好的分布？

做法很干净——把 reward modeling 重新表述为对 p(r | x, y) 的条件密度估计：在冻结的 LLM encoder 之上，用轻量 Diffusion Transformer 从高斯噪声去噪出奖励向量。不对输出分布做任何参数假设，多峰结构自然被表示出来。
一个架构同时吃多属性回归和成对偏好数据；推理时采 N 个样本就是经验奖励分布，可以聚合成标量、方差或分位数。

结果（五个基准）： • 在数据与 backbone 对齐下不弱于基线 • 训练规模相对小，仍能与大得多的判别式 / 分布式 / 生成式 RM 抗衡 • 常规 head 把分布坍缩成一个点时，它能恢复出多峰结构

更实用的是下游：用不确定性做拒绝采样、用 LCB 聚合——而且直接拿 DRM 当 RLHF 训练时的 reward，策略表现更好。这就不只是"更细的评估指标"，而是能直接改善训练。

一句话：奖励不该是一个点，而是一个分布。

Do image models really need a VAE and a separate vision encoder?

NVIDIA researchers released PixelUMM, a 15B-parameter model that handles image and video understanding and generation directly from raw pixels. Images are cut into 16x16 pixel patches and fed into a decoder-only Transformer built on Qwen3-8B, with iterative denoising for generation. That means no VAE compressing images for generation and no pretrained vision encoder for understanding. The code is Apache 2.0, and the checkpoint is licensed for non-commercial research and evaluation only.

For students, this is a great paper to read next to the standard latent-diffusion design, because it makes you ask what each component was buying. Test small text rendering and memory use on your own GPU before forming an opinion. If you want the PyTorch foundations first, my book is here: https://t.co/pbrqeSZ0N0
